scope: All 32 revised audit IDs, including optional bounded improvements; no Hindsight/Evolve, repository split, release publication or deployment.

streams.title: Opchain — Commit verification
sprints: Define the candidate receipt API and policy configuration before coding the verifier. Correct canonical verdict consumption, path quoting, duplicate hook ownership, and PEM scan. Add the audit reproductions as meaningful regression fixtures. Publish the proposed receipt API; do not invent a second checkpoint store.

Implement an executable verifier that tests an immutable effective commit candidate and stores its receipt outside the tree. Bind repository, candidate, policy/toolchain and results. Integrate commit-time verification after mutating hooks; fail closed on missing or mismatched evidence.

Test partial staging, tracked checkpoints, compound commands, substitutions, -C, worktrees, post-check mutation, missing dependencies and combined hook installs. Record which tests are native-host versus script fixtures.

streams.title: Opchain — Release and PR gates
sprints: Separate pre-merge, pre-tag, post-tag and post-deploy verification. Missing mandatory tools/checks produce FAIL or INCOMPLETE. Reconcile local monitoring baseline policy with CI and define a complete version-surface inventory.
No dependencies; do not duplicate A receipt implementation.

Use A receipt and C checkpoint APIs for PR/docs/repo/audit consumers. Required evidence must bind the candidate artifact; compliance stays warn-only. Submit CI/package wiring requests to the coordinator.
Run a disposable release lifecycle and failure-path tests, including absent browsers, bad evidence, all version surfaces, and approved older runtime with newer docs. Do not push a tag or deploy.
streams.scope_guard: Ownership reserves gate-related edits only; unrelated prose in the assigned skill trees is frozen. B1 may read existing CI freely; I owns its changes.

streams.title: Opchain — State, routing and handoffs
sprints: Publish a versioned envelope, typed handoff contracts, lifecycle timestamps and atomic store API. Keep wire 1.1 compatibility; do not introduce 2.0 eval-history changes. Correct natural-language routing and reference retrieval with real-router and MCP-only fixtures.

Implement durable project-scoped local storage, shared validation and concurrency-safe writes. Repair first-use suggestions, invocation normalization, current-run hygiene, finding lifecycle and verification freshness. Maintain hosted session isolation and advisory trust.
Coordinator accepts C1 API; do not edit A gate or E telemetry writer.

Verify reference loading, restart/resume, cross-skill typed reads, interrupted/concurrent writes, first-use suggestions, metadata-only updates and routing coverage. Supply the seven-description publication correction to coordinator packaging.

streams.title: Opchain — Telemetry and PM reliability
sprints: Local consent, privacy and PM identities

Make consent machine-local; validate catalog IDs, verbs and numeric inputs. Separate retries from revised PM events and expand required-contract inventory. Preserve existing data and use synthetic/mocked tests only.
No dependencies; define integration needs against C contract.

Implement reusable rollup/export/event paths with schema-versioned artifacts, denominator handling and privacy suppression. Consume C atomic store for checkpoint writes. Fix fail→pass and changed-contract PM behavior.
Test fresh clone without consent, disable/re-enable, malformed data, aggregation/export, uncertain delivery retry and legitimate revised updates. No external PM messages or data publication.

streams.title: Opchain — Prompt and cost execution
sprints: Reconcile the absent runner with the approved 2.0 runner design without building Hindsight/Evolve. Specify dataset, result, baseline and cost schemas, provider adapter interface and non-authorizing failure states. Implement deterministic grader/core fixtures independently of external credentials.
No dependencies; publish result schema for G/A.

Implement the shared prompt runner and cost CLI, one real provider adapter with mocked network tests, versioned artifacts and nonzero quality/budget exits. Keep provider/model/pricing configurable and explicitly sourced; no live paid calls needed. Submit package script additions to coordinator.
Coordinator accepts F1 schema; integrate C/A APIs only if needed.

Prove candidate versus baseline distinctions, quality regression, budget failure, missing credentials/baselines and interruption. Distinguish deterministic fixtures from live model validation. Produce a migration handoff for the post-split 2.0 plan.

streams.title: Opchain — Reusable execution kits
streams.effort: 5–10 person-days; optional improvement accepted as follow-on scope
sprints: Design opt-in role launcher and data-contract compiler interfaces for one host and one dbt-style adapter. Define immutable inputs, bounded retries, explicit capability limits and dependency manifest. Review-only contract first; do not build another workflow engine, store or eval runner.
No dependencies for contract; implementation waits for A/C/F contracts.

Implement the agreed adapter subset using the shared A/C/F libraries. Reject unsupported dialects/hosts explicitly; validate SQL expressions without claiming universal SQL correctness. Package transitive dependencies through coordinator inventory.
Coordinator releases G2 after A/C/F APIs are stable.
Run from an isolated artifact without authoring-repo/cache imports. Verify separate role inputs, mutation refusal, retry bounds, contract failures and honest runtime/tool isolation labels.

coordinator.title: Current task — Integration and acceptance
sprints: I0: freeze ownership and interface contracts
I1: assemble reviewed changes and regenerate outputs once
I2: capability matrix/diagnostics, artifact-only/native-host journeys and release-readiness report

interface_boundaries.receipt: A owns external verification receipts, candidate identity, policy identity and verifier results. They are not checkpoints and must never be imported from hosted/client-authored state.
interface_boundaries.checkpoint: C owns project state under .checkpoints and its durable local MCP provider, validation, lifecycle and atomic writer. No verification receipt is stored inside its own candidate tree.
interface_boundaries.integration: I owns tests/audit-integration, package/CI wiring and agreement tests between A receipt readers, C state readers and B consumers.
interface_boundaries.eval: F result schema is consumed by G and optional future checks. A does not depend on F to verify ordinary repository checks.

model_policy.escalation: gpt-6-astra only for a specific unresolved issue or focused critical review
